titulo.es: Arabia Saudita invertirá 6.000 millones de euros en tres parques temáticos cerca de París
titulo.en: Saudi Arabia to invest €6 billion in theme parks near Paris, Macron says

sintesis.es: Francia y Arabia Saudita firmaron un acuerdo para una inversión saudita de 6.000 millones de euros (7.000 millones de dólares) destinada a construir tres parques de diversiones cerca de París, uno de ellos posiblemente dedicado al manga. El anuncio se produjo durante la visita del príncipe heredero Mohammed bin Salman a Francia, centrada en acuerdos bilaterales y en la crisis en Medio Oriente.
sintesis.en: France and Saudi Arabia on Monday signed an agreement for the oil-rich Gulf kingdom to invest €6 billion to create three amusement parks near Paris, including one likely to be a manga-themed park, the French presidential office said. The announcement came during Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's visit focused on bilateral deals and the current crisis in the Middle East.

titulo.es: Informe desde Washington: EE. UU. advierte a países que no apoyen sanciones estadounidenses a Irán
titulo.en: Iran predicts ‘another defeat’ for US after Washington's new sanctions

sintesis.es: Estados Unidos lanzó una nueva ofensiva económica contra Irán, pero aún mantiene un período de espera antes de aplicar sanciones más duras a países que comercian con Teherán. La advertencia es clara: aquellos países que no apoyen las sanciones estadounidenses, serían aislados del sistema financiero del dólar. Desde Washington, nuestra corresponsal Carolina Valladares nos cuenta los detalles.
sintesis.en: Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh on Monday warned of "another defeat" for the US after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced expanded sanctions against Tehran. Madanizadeh said Iran had a "two-year plan" to counter the new sanctions and dismissed Bessent's stated efforts to sever "every economic lifeline" sustaining Iran. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

titulo.en: Landslide at waste mound in Guinea capital kills 30, government says

The incident occurred less than a week after the government announced plans to close the ⁠site and relocate the waste because of the threat it posed, especially during the rainy season, which causes landslides and fatal flash ⁠floods each year in crowded, underdeveloped cities across parts of West Africa. titulo.es: How atmospheric dryness limits increases in typhoon rainfall
titulo.en: How atmospheric dryness limits increases in typhoon rainfall

sintesis.es: Under global warming, scientists have widely expected tropical cyclones (including typhoons and hurricanes) to bring more intense and frequent rainfall. The underlying physics seems intuitive: Rising temperatures allow the atmosphere to hold more moisture, which, combined with intensifying storms, should theoretically trigger more destructive downpours. However, when researchers analyze climate model projections, they encounter a puzzling phenomenon.

titulo.es: De la Espriella estrena su política migratoria en Colombia con un anuncio de operativos y deportaciones
titulo.en: Colombia’s new president Abelardo de la Espriella announces immigration crackdown

sintesis.es: El presidente Abelardo de la Espriella ordenó iniciar operativos para identificar y deportar a extranjeros que cometan delitos y a migrantes en situación irregular en Colombia. La medida del ultraderechista marca una de las primeras definiciones de su Gobierno sobre migración en un país donde viven cerca de 2,8 millones de venezolanos, la mayor comunidad de foráneos .
sintesis.en: Far-right leader echoes ally Donald Trump and says operations to ‘track down illegal immigrants’ should begin this week, amid earthquake aftermath Colombia’s far-right president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has announced a crackdown on immigrants, ordering authorities to detain and deport people who are in the country irregularly or have committed crimes. In office for just over two weeks, the millionaire former lawyer made the announcement on Sunday as the country continued to grapple with the aftermath of a 7.4-magnitude earthquake on 10 August that killed more than 300 people and destroyed more than 30,000 homes.
